author: DTrim99
body:
Reconciled — AGI matches at 133,068, and the ~2,600 taxable-income gap is entirely the federal income tax deduction, driven by the federal child credits.

**Reconciliation (taxsimid 201416, IA 2022 HoH, $125,714 wages + $7,355 interest, 1 dependent)**

| IA 1040 step | TaxAct | PolicyEngine |
|---|---|---|
| Net income (line 26/30) | 133,068 | 133,069 |
| Federal tax deduction (line 31) | 19,616 | **17,016.57** |
| Standard deduction (line 37) | 5,450 | 5,450 |
| **Taxable income (line 38)** | **108,002** | **110,602** |

The $19,616 you entered as withholding is PolicyEngine's **federal income tax _before_ credits** (the "Federal Income Tax Before Credits" line in the emulator output). But the amount PE deducts for Iowa is the federal income tax **liability** — `fiitax`, i.e. _after_ the $2,000 child tax credit and the $600 child-and-dependent-care credit:

```
19,616.57 (before credits) − 2,000 (CTC) − 600 (CDCC) = 17,016.57  ("Federal IIT Liability")
```

That's exactly the 2,600 gap. PolicyEngine's Iowa deduction ([`ia_fedtax_deduction`](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/blob/main/policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/ia/tax/income/including_married_filing_separately/deductions/ia_fedtax_deduction.py)) uses `income_tax_before_refundable_credits` — the federal tax net of the nonrefundable child credits (the liability), not the pre-credit figure.

So on the liability basis TAXSIM and PE both use, the number to put in the TA Q&A is **17,016** (fiitax), not 19,616; with that, TaxAct's line 31 and taxable income land at 17,016 / 110,602, matching PE. (19,616 is the correct _withholding_ on a cash/paid basis — that's the liability-vs-paid difference you noted — but the child credits make the liability 2,600 lower than that withholding.)

One thing to confirm on your side: does TAXSIM's Iowa federal-tax deduction also net out the federal CTC/CDCC (use 17,016)? If so, this fully reconciles. If TAXSIM instead keeps the pre-credit 19,616, then the real question is whether Iowa's federal-tax deduction should be reduced by the federal child credits — happy to run that down in the Iowa instructions if that's where it's pointing.
